summary: F1: A phishing-suspect mail was delivered to n.guler@aegean.edu from aegean-edu.com.tr (subject: Ekim maaş bordrosu düzeltmesi – IBAN güncelleme) [T1566.002]. Risk Gate escalates at confidence 0.8 based on one access signal; no confirmed abuse chain was established.

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 (firmware 22.7R2.3) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: vpn-edge-01 did not carry a sign-in for n.guler@aegean.edu; its KEV status is not relevant to this account's exposure

actions.action: Block sender domain aegean-edu.com.tr and the phishing subject line at the mail gateway; hunt all mailboxes for duplicate messages.
Force password reset for n.guler@aegean.edu and inspect sign-in logs, mailbox rules, and forwarding for unauthorized activity.
Notify the user not to interact with the message and provide IBAN-change verification guidance via trusted channels.

limitations:
Limited to one confirmed finding (F1); no abuse chain beyond initial email delivery was established.
VPN appliance KEV/CVE claims were rejected and add no account-level context.
Escalation reason: signals of compromise without a confirmed abuse chain
not_checked:
Post-delivery user interaction (link clicks, credential submission) and mailbox audit trails after delivery.
Endpoint EDR alerts on the user workstation associated with the phishing email.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F1 would leave no surviving signal and the policy would land on benign — the opposite of the human-review path we chose.

risk.rationale: F1 is a CONFIRMED (0.8) phishing-suspect email delivered to n.guler@aegean.edu (T1566.002, financial IBAN/salary lure), which constitutes confirmed exposure but not a confirmed account takeover chain — there is no evidence of credential entry, suspicious sign-in, mailbox modification, or downstream misuse. The VPN-appliance KEV claim was explicitly rejected as irrelevant to this account, and there are no data-quality conflicts. Because the signal is confirmed rather than weak/unexplained (not monitor), not explained away (not benign), and lacks confirmed takeover evidence (not contain), the appropriate gate outcome is escalate: a human must determine whether the user interacted with the message and whether containment is required. Cited confirmed finding: F1.
escalate_reasons: signals of compromise without a confirmed abuse chain
